headline: CENTINELA COPPER STRIKE OFFICIALLY BEGINS — CHINA POST-HOLIDAY BUYING DRIVES REBOUND TO $6.57/LB
snippet: LME copper rebounded to approximately $6.57 per pound ($14,490/t) on October 9 as Chinese buyers re-entered the market following the Golden Week holiday, reversing the prior session's demand-fear selloff to $14,300/t. Simultaneously, Antofagasta's Centinela mine in Chile officially commenced a strike, adding genuine supply-risk premium to the recovery — a combination of demand catalyst and supply disruption that analysts say is exactly the setup that can generate sharp short squeezes in copper futures.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 2026 LOW AT CNY 122,350/T — STOCKPILE REVISION EXTENDS SEPTEMBER'S 20%+ ROUT
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate fell a further 2.08% on October 9 to CNY 122,350 per tonne, sliding below the CNY 123,000 level that had defined the year-to-date floor after a downward revision to official stockpile data prompted a round of liquidation. The move extends a brutal September in which lithium carbonate shed more than a fifth of its value, and underscores that demand from EV makers in the US and Europe has not yet arrived in sufficient volume to clear the supply overhang built by Chinese production expansion.

headline: SILVER SURGES 2.1% TO $60.40 AS GOLD-SILVER RATIO TIGHTENS TO 69 — METALS RECOVER IN TANDEM
snippet: Silver gained 2.06% to $60.40 per troy ounce on October 9 while gold climbed roughly 1.4% to approximately $4,191, tightening the gold-to-silver ratio from Thursday's 70:1 divergence to approximately 69.36. The combined recovery signals a partial reversal of the industrial-demand concerns that drove silver's relative weakness earlier in the week, with analysts noting the move suggests silver is benefiting from both the monetary bid lifting gold and a rebound in Chinese base-metals sentiment post-Golden Week.

headline: CHINA DEMANDS COPPER SUPPLY TERMS TO CLEAR $54B ANGLO-TECK MERGER — SOLE HOLDOUT BEFORE MARCH 2027 CLOSE
snippet: Anglo American's CEO said October 7 that the proposed $54 billion merger with Canada's Teck Resources has cleared every regulatory jurisdiction except China, where authorities are negotiating copper supply commitments as their closing condition — a demand that illustrates how resource nationalism and supply-chain security have become standard elements of major cross-border mining approvals. Both companies expect the transaction to close by March 2027; the CEO described the current deal environment as 'new waters' for the industry.

headline: MMG BLASTS EU ANTITRUST CASE ON ANGLO NICKEL — "BLOCKING DEAL CLOSES THE MINE," SELLER WARNS
snippet: MMG, the Chinese-Australian miner, formally challenged the European Commission's statement of objections against its $500 million acquisition of Anglo American's Brazilian nickel business, accusing EU regulators of ignoring evidence that the deal would not divert nickel supplies from Europe to China. Anglo American backed MMG's position, warning that a blocked deal would likely force the closure of the Brazilian mine entirely — removing supply from the global market rather than protecting European access to it.

headline: TOP 50 MINING COMPANIES SHED $264 BILLION AS GOLD TRADE UNWINDS AND LITHIUM STOCKS EXIT
snippet: Mining.com's latest ranking of the world's 50 largest mining companies by market capitalization shows the cohort has collectively shed approximately $264 billion in value as momentum in gold miners reverses from summer highs and lithium equities extend their decline alongside falling battery-metal prices. The sector's leadership is increasingly concentrated in royalty and streaming companies and diversified majors with copper exposure, while single-commodity gold and lithium pure-plays account for the majority of the loss.

headline: MIDAS MINERALS T-13 NAMIBIA: 22.6M AT 6.01% CUEQ FROM 347M — HIGH-GRADE COPPER-SILVER DISCOVERY GROWS
snippet: Midas Minerals (ASX: MM1) reported that hole T-13 at its Namibia copper project returned 22.6 metres averaging 6.01% copper equivalent — comprising 4.67% copper and 70.9 g/t silver — from 347.5 metres depth. The result significantly exceeds initial discovery grades and, at that depth and width combination, indicates potential for an underground bulk-tonnage target at economic copper-equivalent values with meaningful silver by-product credit.

headline: CASCADIA MINERALS CARMACKS: 75.55M AT 1.19% CU, 0.97 G/T AU — YUKON PORPHYRY BLOWS PAST HISTORIC PIT BOUNDARIES
snippet: Cascadia Minerals reported drill hole CD-26-058 at its Carmacks project in Yukon intersected 75.55 metres grading 1.19% copper, 0.97 g/t gold, 10.4 g/t silver and 335 ppm molybdenum — a polymetallic interval extending mineralization well beyond the historic resource and pit shell. The 1.19% copper grade over 75+ metres of continuous width is among the better near-surface porphyry results in Yukon in 2026 and reinforces Carmacks' position in an increasingly active Canadian copper corridor.

headline: EQUITY METALS SILVER QUEEN: 2.6M AT 844 G/T AGEQUIVALENT — BC HIGH-GRADE SILVER CONTINUITY CONFIRMED IN VALIDATION DRILLING
snippet: Equity Metals (TSXV: EQMEF) released assays from 2026 validation drilling at the Silver Queen property in British Columbia, returning a headline interval of 2.6 metres averaging 844 g/t silver equivalent — confirming high-grade continuity in the deposit's No. 3 vein system. Up to eight additional holes totalling 2,500 metres are planned to define dilution and advance Silver Queen toward a resource update, with drilling expected to resume the second week of October.

headline: CHINA NOVEMBER RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROLS LOOM — FIRST REAL TEST OF WESTERN REFINING AND RECYCLING CAPACITY
snippet: A new round of Chinese rare earth export control measures set to take effect in November 2026 will serve as the first genuine test of whether Western rare earth refining and recycling capacity has grown enough to absorb the constraint without triggering price spikes, according to analysts at Fastmarkets. The controls arrive as US critical minerals policy faces a potential pivot ahead of midterm elections and a planned Trump-Xi meeting, injecting added policy uncertainty into an already supply-disrupted market for neodymium, dysprosium and other magnet metals.

headline: UBS NAMES TOP GOLD MINERS ON CASH RETURNS — COBRE PANAMA RESTART "MOSTLY UNPRICED," ENDEAVOUR AT 10%+ FCF YIELD
snippet: A fresh UBS gold mining sector note selects top names based on improving operational performance, near-term cash returns and valuation support, while flagging rising 2027 cost pressures as the sector's key risk. UBS highlights Endeavour Mining as trading at above a 10% spot free cash flow yield — attributed to elevated country-risk discount — and identifies the Cobre Panama mine restart as 'mostly unpriced' in the sector, representing an asymmetric catalyst if Panama's regulatory path clears.

headline: ESKAY MINING WRAPS 3,638M OF 2026 GOLDEN TRIANGLE DRILLING — ASSAYS PENDING ON BC'S HISTORIC HIGH-GRADE CAMP
snippet: Eskay Mining (TSX: ESK) announced completion of its 2026 diamond drilling program at the Eskay Creek property in BC's Golden Triangle, totalling 3,638 metres across multiple high-priority targets. Laboratory assays are now pending, with results expected to determine whether the 2026 program has extended known high-grade zones at one of Canada's historically richest precious metals camps — the original Eskay Creek mine produced gold and silver at extraordinary grades from 1994 to 2008.
